full_judgment:
The opposite parties as plaintiffs filed T.S. No. 361 of 1982 on 31.8.82 in the 2nd Court of Munsif, Barisal for establishment of title and for confirmation of possession and/or recovery of khas possession in the suit property as described in the schedule of the plaint. The suit was subsequently transferred to the Court of Addl. Asstt. Judge, 2nd court, Barisal and renumbered as T.S. No. 122 of 1990. The plaintiffs case is that Jabberallah was the recorded tenant of the suit property and he died leaving only one son Mofizuddin, the plaintiffs are the heirs of Mofizuddin and the plaintiff No. 1 used to reside in different places in connection with his service and his cousin Abdul Motaleb was entrusted to look after the suit property. After retirement, the plaintiff himself took over possession of the suit property, but at the time of payment of rent he came to know that Abdul Motaleb fraudulently managed to create a record of right in respect of the suit property in the name of his father in law, Sonamuddin. 

 3. The plaintiff thereafter reported the matter to the village court for necessary action but without any result, and subsequently he requested the heirs of Sonamuddin to revert back the property but to no effect and thereafter the plaintiff instituted the suit. Subsequently plaintiffs brought an application for amendment on 21.5.90 for inserting a prayer for recovery of khas possession and the amendment was allowed by the learned trial court. 

 7. Mr. Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate for the petitioner. has submitted that the plaintiffs could not prove their title and possession in the suit property, as it appears from the evidence on record and the possession of the plaintiff predecessor in the suit land has also not been proved and the possession of the defendants having been admitted by the P.W. 1 the plaintiff himself in his deposition in cross examination the learned trial court rightly dismissed the suit having regard to the materials on record, and therefore the order of remand is not proper order under the provision of law. He has further submitted that the plaintiff’s possession at any point of time having not been proved the suit for confirmation of possession and or for recovery of khas possession is in competent. His further submission is that there is no averment either in the plaint or in the amendment petition that the plaintiffs were dispossessed by the defendant from the suit land. He has further argued that the learned appellate court without adverting to the findings of facts on title and possession of the plaintiffs in the suit property and without arriving at an independent finding in that respect upon assessment of the evidence, erroneously held that the plaint was not well prepared and an opportunity may be given to the plaintiff for amendment of the plaint, in the above view his submission is that the remand order cannot be sustained in law. 

 9. From the judgment of the trial court it clearly appears that admittedly Jabborullah was the C.S. recorded tenant and according to the plaint case the plaintiffs inherited the suit land from the heirs of Jabborullah. In the R.S. Operation as well as in S.A. operation neither the plaintiffs names nor the name of their predecessor Mofizuddin has been recorded and for the last 40 years or so no record of right has ever been prepared in the name of any of the plaintiffs. Admittedly the record of right was prepared in the name of Sonamuddin son of Arman Mutaiat. It is the finding of the trial court that the plaintiffs failed to prove that Abdul Motaleb used to look after the suit land and paid rent, as no rent receipt showing payment of rent in respect of the suit property during the long period has been filed before the court. Considering the deposition of P.W.1 the plaintiff the finding of trial court is that the plaintiff admitted that the defendant is have their homestead in plot no. 4673 and the plaintiffs did not see their father to possess the suit land. It is also admitted by the plaintiff in cross examination that he does not live on the land comprising the suit plot and he has prayed for khas possession of the entire suit land. Considering the evidence of P.W.1 the trial court found that the plaintiffs had never been in possession of the suit land and the defendant No. 11 has homestead comprising .19 decimal and the said portion of the land is possessed by the defendant No. 11. Trial court further found that from the evidence of P.W. 1 the plaintiff, it reveals that Safayet defendant No. 11 and Shoukat built their houses on one of the suit plots and the plaintiff at the age of 10/12 years left Barisal and he had always been out of Barisal and he came back to Barisal in the year of 1977, and thus it is proved that for the last 40/50 years the plaintiffs had no physical connection with the suit property. The plaintiffs possession could not otherwise be proved. In evidence the plaintiffs claimed .33 decimals of land and abandoned the claim over 19 decimal of land in favour of defendant No. 11. Thus the Trial court has conclusively found that the plaintiffs have no title in the suit land and they had never been in possession of the suit land and further defendant possession is admitted by the plain-tiff. The suit was accordingly dismissed. 

 11. In a suit for establishment of title and recovery of khas possession the plaintiff first prove his title by evidence and then plaintiffs possession to a certain point of lime has to be dearly proved. If the plaintiffs possession is proved then comes the question of dispossession. how and when the defendants dispossessed the plaintiff. But the learned Dist. Judge, unfortunately failed to discuss the material evidence as to the possession and title of the plaintiffs and consequently the findings as to the plaintiffs title and possession arrived at by the trial court have not been reversed.
